name: Street Custom 'Widowmaker' Rigged Power Tool
description: Any standard power tool — circular saw, angle grinder, reciprocating saw, drill — modified for use as a weapon by removing safety guards, locking the trigger in the on position, and in some cases extending the blade or bit for reach. Widowmakers are the weapons of people who cannot afford weapons but have access to a job site. The most common variant is an angle grinder with the guard removed and a cutting disc replaced with a diamond blade, capable of cutting through body armor and bone with equal efficiency. The psychological impact of an attacker running at you with a screaming power tool is significant — it is loud, sprays sparks, and communicates a level of commitment that discourages engagement.
legality: Prohibited when modified — modified power tool as weapon
specifications:
tool type: Variable — angle grinder, circular saw, reciprocating saw, drill
blade/bit: Standard industrial, often upgraded to diamond or carbide
power source: Tool's original battery or corded
weight: 1.5-5 kg depending on tool
modification: Guard removal, trigger lock, extended blade
effective range: Arm's reach
noise: 85-110 dB — extremely loud
story_hooks: A construction crew moonlighting as enforcers uses Widowmakers exclusively — their attacks look like workplace accidents and the weapons are their legitimate work tools.
A Tier 1 gladiatorial event features Widowmaker combat — fighters armed with modified power tools in a steel cage, and the audience is placing bets through corporate gambling networks.
related_entities: NeuralPath LinkGuard Secure Civic Identity BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist industrial tool stripped of its safety skin — exposed spinning mechanism, jagged cutting surface, bare metal frame. Looks like something salvaged from a construction site and weaponized with surgical precision. The absence of guards makes its danger immediately obvious.
physical_description.dimensions: Angle grinder variant: 23cm length × 12cm width × 10cm height. Blade diameter 125mm (standard industrial) to 180mm (modified variants). Reciprocating saw variant extends to 45cm total length.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced — 2.5-3.5kg depending on variant. Feels substantial in the hand, requiring a firm two-handed grip. The motor vibration is palpable even at rest.
physical_description.primary_material: Stamped steel chassis, aluminum alloy motor housing, carbon fiber reinforced polymer body panels (some variants stripped to bare metal). Cutting disc is carbide or industrial-grade diamond.
physical_description.finish: Weathered industrial — worn factory paint over bare steel, spark-scored metal, polymer panels scuffed and discolored from site use. Some show crude duct tape wraps on grip areas. No attempt at cosmetic concealment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey and burnt orange (rust bleeding through worn finish). Black polymer panels. Blade surfaces are silver-grey with heat scorching.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare knurled metal or thick industrial rubber grip, often augmented with wrapped electrical tape, paracord, or medical wrap for improved purchase during violence. Sweaty palms leave visible marks.
distinctive_features: Safety guard completely removed — exposed motor and spinning mechanism
Trigger mechanism permanently locked or cable-tied in 'on' position
Extended blade/bit for increased reach (3-5cm beyond standard)
Spark deflector jury-rigged from steel plate or removed entirely
Motor vents showing carbon buildup from extended use
Crude welded reinforcement around blade mount
Battery indicator (if cordless) visible and often taped over
Wear patterns showing repeated high-impact contact
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Original tool manufacturer stamp (DeWalt, Makita, Bosch) visible on motor housing, partially obscured by wear or intentionally ground down. No Street Custom branding — this is purely a field modification.
physical_description.condition_typical: Battle-worn field tool. Scuff marks, dent patterns, discoloration from repeated high-speed contact. Blade typically shows microchipping or heat damage. Grip tape fraying. Battery terminals corroded if cordless variant. Bloodstain cleanup attempts visible as discoloration.
